Subject: Recap + next steps — Performance SLOs & multi-region routing

Thanks Sam & Priya — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same picture:

Summary of requirements (as discussed)
- Latency targets: p95 <= 120ms (US), p95 <= 120ms (EU), p95 <= 220ms (APAC) for token-complete responses.
- Throughput: sustained 500 req/s with spikes to 750 req/s (peak).
- Concurrency: expected user concurrency ~200 (total across frontends); per-instance concurrency target to size autoscaling.
- Streaming: token-level streaming is required for the primary product path (server-to-client chunked responses).
- Data residency: EU customer data and logs must remain in EU region; APAC data should stay in APAC region where possible (GDPR & local compliance considerations).

Open/Action items
1) Redwood to validate these targets with a short perf test plan and recommend model/quantization variants and routing config (due: Aug 12). Attachment: load_test_plan.xlsx
2) Aditya to provide technical notes on regional routing, caching, and streaming implications (cc'ed).
3) Finova to confirm any stricter data residency needs (e.g., cross-border backups) and provide point of contact for infra/infosec.
4) Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive with Finova infra team — propose next Wed/Thu.

If this matches your notes, we can kick off the perf validation and propose a 2-week POC with dedicated capacity in EU + APAC edge points.

Best,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing internally:

- Latency: Our product owners are comfortable with p95 <= 120ms for US/EU. APAC target can be relaxed to p95 <= 220ms given regional infra, but lower is better.
- Throughput/Concurrency: We should size for sustained 750 req/s during business hours with spikes up to 1,000 req/s for peak events. Concurrency of 200 is the right ballpark for now; we may need headroom for bursts.
- Streaming: Yes, token streaming is required — it's critical for perceived latency for end-users.
- Data residency: EU data must remain within EU. We also need to ensure logs/analytics that contain PII are kept in-region; please confirm whether audit logs can be partitioned per-region. Compliance team will share details if needed.

Questions:
1) If a regional endpoint is down, can routing fail over to another region without moving EU data out of EU?
2) What encryption-at-rest options do you offer for Dedicated/Private deployments (KMS/HSM)?

We'll also loop in our infra lead (Priya) to set up the tech dive.

—Sam

Thanks Sam — helpful clarifications. Quick answers while Aditya adds the technical detail:
- Failover: we can route by policy to avoid exporting EU-resident data. Typical pattern is to failover traffic metadata (e.g., requests from EU can fall back to a compatible EU-hosted model variant or a cached prefix in EU). Full failover to a non-EU region (e.g., US) would only be used for non-PII requests and requires explicit agreement.
- Encryption: we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private deployments; HSM-backed keys are available for private/per-customer infra.

Next steps: Aditya — can you add a short note on routing patterns, expected P95 impact from batching/cache, and suggested autoscaling parameters? Once we have that, we'll propose the POC scope and dates.

Hi Sam / team — quick technical note to address the routing and perf questions:

1) Regional routing options
- Geo-based routing: route by user IP/region to nearest regional endpoint (EU, US, APAC). This preserves residency for data in flight and storage.
- Policy-based routing: route by account/tenant metadata so specific tenants always hit EU region regardless of IP. Useful for corporate VPN traffic.
- Failover: we recommend a phased failover where cached prefixes or read-only responses can be served from a nearby region; full request handling can only be failed over with consent for data residency exceptions.

2) Latency impact: batching and KV/prefix caching reduce per-token cost but add a small queuing delay. For p95 <= 120ms we recommend:
- Keep batch windows under 5ms for real-time paths; use continuous batching with small max batch sizes (8–16) for most models.
- Aggressive KV/prefix caching for hot prompts — this can yield sub-50ms token-generation on optimized kernels.

3) Concurrency & autoscaling guidance
- Baseline instance type for POC: 4xA100-equivalent GPU workers per pool (or equivalent for cloud) with per-worker concurrency target of ~16–32 in streaming mode.
- For 750 req/s sustained with streaming and average 40 tokens per response, plan for an initial pool of 10–16 workers and autoscale threshold at 70% CPU/GPU utilization.

4) Streaming specifics
- We support server-sent events (SSE) and HTTP chunked responses. Streaming adds a small per-connection overhead; keep keep-alives and connection pooling in front of the service.

Attachments included: perf_baseline_20260810.pdf (baseline numbers from similar workloads), redwood_slo_proposal.docx (draft SLOs).

I'll prepare a short perf test run (scripts + config) and share results by EOD Aug 12 so we can scope the POC.
